questions.enonce_markdown: Draw the set up for the experiment. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*What to draw and label:*

1. A **burette** held vertically by a **clamp on a retort stand**, containing the **dilute HCl**, with its tap at the bottom.
2. Below the burette tip, a **conical flask** standing on a **white tile** (to see the colour change), containing **25 cm$^3$ of 0.20 M NaOH** (taken with the pipette) and a few drops of **phenolphthalein** (pink).
3. Labels: burette, dilute HCl, clamp, stand, conical flask, NaOH + phenolphthalein, white tile.

questions.enonce_markdown:
25 cm$^3$ of 0.20M NaOH was transferred into the conical flask and 3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator were added.

(i) Name the apparatus used in transferring 0.20M NaOH into the conical flask. ......... *[1 mark]*

(ii) State the colour change in the conical flask. From ......... To ......... *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **(25 cm$^3$) pipette**, used with a pipette filler.

(ii) Phenolphthalein is pink in an alkali (NaOH) and colourless in an acid. The colour changes from **pink** to **colourless** when the acid has just neutralised the alkali (end point).

questions.enonce_markdown:
The dilute acid was run from the burette and the results were recorded as shown in the following table:

| | Approximate | First accurate | Second accurate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Final burette reading | 26.2 cm$^3$ | 46.0 cm$^3$ | 49.0 cm$^3$ |
| Initial burette reading | 0.2 cm$^3$ | 20.9 cm$^3$ | 24.1 cm$^3$ |
| Titre/cm$^3$ | | | |

(i) Complete the table above

(ii) Determine the mean titre. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Titre = final reading - initial reading:

| | Approximate | First accurate | Second accurate |
|---|---|---|---|
| Final burette reading | 26.2 cm$^3$ | 46.0 cm$^3$ | 49.0 cm$^3$ |
| Initial burette reading | 0.2 cm$^3$ | 20.9 cm$^3$ | 24.1 cm$^3$ |
| Titre/cm$^3$ | **26.0** | **25.1** | **24.9** |

(ii) The approximate titre is only a rough guide and is not used. The two accurate titres (25.1 and 24.9 cm$^3$) agree to within 0.2 cm$^3$, so their mean is the mean titre:

$\dfrac{25.1 + 24.9}{2} = \mathbf{25.0\ cm^3}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Calculate the concentration of the acid if 25cm$^3$ of 0.20M NaOH was required.

$\mathrm{NaOH(aq)} + \mathrm{HCl(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl(aq)} + \mathrm{H_2O(l)}$ *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Moles of NaOH: $n = c \times V = 0.20 \times \dfrac{25}{1000} = 0.0050\ \mathrm{mol}$.

From the equation, NaOH and HCl react in the ratio 1 : 1, so $n(\mathrm{HCl}) = 0.0050\ \mathrm{mol}$ in the mean titre of $25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

Concentration of the acid: $c = \dfrac{n}{V} = \dfrac{0.0050}{25.0/1000} = \mathbf{0.20\ mol\,dm^{-3}}$ (0.20 M).
